title: batchMint forfeits dispatcher-side slippage protection by passing empty extraData on every iteration
description: BatchNFTMinter calls the no-extraData overload of `ITokenMinter.mint`. The interface NatSpec documents `extraData` as dispatcher-specific slippage parameters. The BalancerPooler dispatcher routes payment through a Balancer pool swap; without slippage params the swap accepts whatever the pool quotes at execution time. Single-mint callers can choose the extraData overload and pass slippage bounds; batch callers cannot reach it. As a result every iteration in the loop performs an unprotected pool swap.
impact: Caller's prepaid `paymentAmount` is exposed to MEV sandwich attacks on the Balancer pool leg. Unlike M-02 sibling DEDUP-002 (gas-only via atomic revert), here the dispatcher can succeed at a worse pool execution price — the mint completes, but a larger fraction of `paymentAmount` is consumed per mint than the user expected at submission time. The single-mint extraData overload exists precisely to bound this; batch callers are denied feature parity. Aggregate loss scales with batch size and pool depth and can dwarf per-iteration price growth.
attackPath: Honest user calls batchMint(count=N, paymentAmount=P) intending to receive N NFTs at the current pool-quoted cost
MEV searcher front-runs with a Balancer swap that moves the pool against the user's payment direction
Inside each loop iteration, BalancerPoolerV2 dispatcher swaps the user's payment-token at the now-degraded pool quote (no slippage params to revert with)
Each mint succeeds at a higher effective price; cumulative cost approaches paymentAmount — user receives N NFTs but pays substantially more than the spot-quoted price would have implied
Searcher back-runs to capture the pool imbalance
recommendation: Add an `extraData` (single shared) or `bytes[] calldata extraDatas` (per-iteration) parameter to `batchMint` and forward to the slippage-aware mint overload. If M-01 is fixed by switching to V2, route through `ITokenMinterV2.mint(uint256,address,bytes)` to preserve slippage bounds in the migrated path.
severityRationale: KEEP at medium. C4 Medium fits: 'Assets not at direct risk, but the function of the protocol... could be impacted, or leak value with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements.' The assumption (Balancer-pool-routing dispatcher) and external requirement (MEV-active mempool) are both satisfied by current production wiring. Distinct from L-01 / DEDUP-002: here actual paymentAmount is consumed at worse-than-quoted prices (atomic-rollback does NOT save the user because the swap simply succeeds at a degraded rate), so the loss is real value extraction not just gas. Note: this finding is conditioned on M-01 being fixed (V2 retargeting) — once retargeted, the V2 mint(uint256,address,bytes) overload still needs to be used, and the same mitigation framing applies.
